source.title: A Refresh Interval Does Not Fully Specify a Refresh Schedule: Learning-Rate-Dependent Placement in Kronecker-Preconditioned Language Model Training
source.authors: Xin-Yu Wang; Zhi-Wei Zhai; Yu Gu; Zi-Jun Yu; Sicheng Lyu; Jing-Rui Tian; Lei Ding; Zi-Yang Song; Xiao-Wen Chang McGill University; The Chinese University of Hong Kong; University of Manitoba; O. University

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no obvious cutoff or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures held-out loss under changes to optimizer refresh placement, learning rate, model size, and training horizon. It does not measure training error or the train–test gap, and does not test the listed versions directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out language-model NLL differences across refresh schedules, but does not report training error or a generalization gap. It therefore does not test the claim that networks fitting arbitrary labels generalize on natural labels, or any listed version. Results below are relevant to held-out performance and are recorded as findings for none of the versions. Cited optimizer and refresh-frequency results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares refresh schedules within Mousse, rather than any intervention or comparison specified by V1–V8. Its discussion of tuning-dependent optimizer rankings cites V4 sources, but it does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD. Held-out NLL alone is not the disqualifier; the tested comparison does not match a claim version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: in short-horizon Mousse language-model training, fixed-count refresh placement changes held-out loss, and its preferred placement depends on learning rate, model size and training length. The authors recommend reporting complete schedules, comparing relevant learning rates and including an equal-budget uniform reference. They also conclude that spectral-width drift fails to predict the placement reversal.
record.recipe_differences: Studies refresh placement within Mousse at fixed refresh counts, rather than random-label memorization/generalization or the interventions in the listed versions. The implementation also differs from published Mousse internals, with a joint-restoration control.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured placement contrast varies with learning rate, corpus, model size, training horizon, refresh density, and jointly restored optimizer internals.

fits_no_version.finding: At fixed refresh count, placement changes held-out NLL. On FineWeb, the preferred mirrored placement reverses with learning rate; other corpora have different rankings. Uniform placement beats the better mirrored schedule on five of six corpora at mirrored-pair tuned rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refresh placement within Mousse can affect held-out language-model loss at fixed refresh compute, with rankings dependent on learning rate and corpus.

fits_no_version.finding: The schedule-preference boundary falls across the model-size ladder, falls faster than the uniform-schedule loss-optimal learning rate, and changes with training horizon.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mousse refresh-schedule rankings require rechecking across model sizes and training horizons.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral-width drift predicts earlier placement in every surface cell and misses observed reversals; mean within-corpus rank correlation is −.667. Appendix E also reports training and evaluation contrasts agreeing with correlation .88.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested scalar curvature-drift statistic does not reliably predict refresh-placement rankings, and the observed placement contrast is not explained as a generalization-only effect.

record.code_released: Anonymized supplementary material; no URL stated.
record.problems: Short-horizon training; one optimizer; size and tokens per parameter vary together across the main scale ladder. Independent cohorts at fixed sizes differed more than within-cohort seed variation. Some highest-rate results were seed-inconsistent or near the stability margin. Attempts to extend to other optimizers were inconclusive. The study does not measure training error or the train–test gap.
record.rows_left_out: The full 30-cell corpus-by-learning-rate surface is in Table 4; only the FineWeb reversal cells and tuned-rate effects for each corpus are included. Other budget-8 and budget-16 cell medians, auxiliary AdamW-rate comparisons (Table 6), per-size independent-cohort values and horizon details for 64M are omitted because they are additional numeric cells beyond the selected coverage. The spectral-width score results and earlier staleness-account tests are not entered as rows because they concern a predictor of schedule ranking, not a measured train–test gap or listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization and chance-level held-out performance with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, optimizer switching and decoupled-weight-decay recovery.
Large versus small minibatches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their performance difference.
Dropout effects, small-data and excessive-dropout regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap ranking and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and measuring test-accuracy changes.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's categorical assertion that training performance is not measured: Appendix E, Table 8 reports agreement between training and evaluation contrasts (correlation .88). This does not test any listed version. Spectral width is not V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness. Omitted spectral diagnostics and additional numeric cells are already declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the stated tuning protocols.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and weight-decay effects on test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: GPT-350M
rows.operation_detail: Moved the middle refresh pair among five centers, keeping refresh budget, endpoints, and separation fixed.
rows.measure: Endpoint held-out NLL relative to centre 251
rows.baseline: Centre 251
rows.value: At the lowest rate the earliest centre was worst; at the highest rate it was best; the intermediate landscape was nearly flat.
rows.note: The paper says the highest-rate end-to-end tilt exceeded tie tolerance by an order of magnitude.
rows.check: The learning-rate condition is incomplete: Figure 3 compares .012, .016 and .024, not only .012. The row aggregates their different outcomes and measures no listed version.

rows.note: The paper says the reversal is unresolved at this density.
rows.check: Valid aggregate schedule finding, but it measures no listed version; placement effects are established while a dense-schedule reversal remains unresolved.
